title: November 2nd the Longest Day
description: The longest surviving November 2 recording follows an overnight DVDASA and Mangchi production from reunions and wrestling through band planning, trivia, fan stories, a proposed wedding, and an exhausted musical close.
summary: The longest surviving November 2 recording follows an overnight DVDASA and Mangchi production from reunions and wrestling through band planning, trivia, fan stories, a proposed wedding, and an exhausted musical close. At more than four hours in the current reader timeline, it is a composite-feeling live-day document rather than a conventional interview. David Choe, Asa Akira, Bobby Lee, Khalyla, Steve Lee, Money Mark, Critter Fleming, Bobby Trivia and other public guests rotate through the room. Early sections revisit friendship between the Lee brothers, put Steve into physical and sexualized demonstrations, and assess Mangchi's first live response. David and the band debate whether touring is feasible, whether backing tracks could substitute for a full band, and how Steve's work ethic, health and audience draw affect future plans. The middle becomes an explicit body-image and adult-industry roundtable. Participants discuss labiaplasty, performer insecurity, body dysmorphia, sexual technique and relationship jealousy. Direct refusals during physical demonstrations remain refusals; the editorial layer does not convert jokes, employment, fandom or an adult-performer identity into permission. Bobby Trivia then runs a substantial formal trivia game, correcting the false impression that trivia existed only in the small curated subset. Later arrivals include a Korean travel account, filmmakers and fans who explain how DVDASA affected their collaborations and relationships. A couple who met through the show discuss an onstage wedding; David says he has been ordained and frames marriage seriously despite the surrounding spectacle. The last movement turns to pornography, truthfulness and a disputed off-site incident, including a caller who is pressured to produce evidence and admits lying during a speakerphone confrontation. Those claims are preserved as contested live testimony, not adjudicated fact. The archive withholds private partners, contact paths and intimate identifying details, and does not infer cast from every voice in the crowded room. The closing rough song includes alien-abduction and disability language. The automatic transcript has no validated speaker turns, so the extensive entity context is route-level only.
